verses.text: Look, my eyes have seen all this. My ears have heard it and understood it.
What you know, I also know. I am not less than you.
But I want to speak to the Almighty. I want to argue my case with God.
As for you, you cover things up with lies. You are all worthless doctors.
If only you would keep completely quiet! That would be the wise thing for you to do.
Now listen to my argument. Pay attention to what I have to say.
Will you tell lies for God? Will you speak falsely for him?
Will you take his side? Will you argue his case for him?
Would it go well for you if he looked closely at you? Can you fool him the way you fool people?
He would surely correct you if you secretly took sides.
Wouldn't his greatness frighten you? Wouldn't the fear of him fall on you?
Your wise sayings are as useless as ashes. Your arguments are as weak as clay.
Be quiet and let me speak! Then let whatever happens to me happen.
Why should I put myself in danger and take my life in my own hands?
Even if he kills me, and I have no hope, I will still defend my ways in front of him.
This might even save me, because no godless person would dare to come before him.
Listen carefully to my words. Let what I say ring in your ears.
Look, I have prepared my case, and I know I will be proved right.
Can anyone bring charges against me? If so, I will be quiet and die.
God, grant me just two things, and then I will not hide from you:
take your hand away from me, and stop frightening me with your terrors.
Then call me, and I will answer. Or let me speak, and you answer me.
How many wrongs and sins have I done? Show me my rebellion and my sin.
Why do you hide your face from me and treat me like your enemy?
Will you frighten a leaf blown by the wind? Will you chase after dry straw?
You write down bitter charges against me and make me pay for the sins I did when I was young.
You put my feet in chains and watch every step I take. You draw a line around where my feet may go.
So I waste away like something rotten, like clothing eaten by moths.
